historical_record.description: Before the 1906 earthquake the corner lot held a two-storey saloon with a grocery store, about 45 by 50 feet, then numbered 346–350 12th Street; a one-storey dwelling faced Harrison Street on the rear lot.
The present one-storey wood-frame corner building went up; its architect and builder are unknown.
The one-storey corner building was a saloon, then numbered 350 12th Street, with a storage shed next door at 348A.
From about the 1950s to the mid-1970s the corner building housed Buzz’s Shamrock Inn Tavern; it then stood empty until 1980.
The San Francisco Eagle, a leather bar, opened here in 1982 and traded into the early 1990s.
Work began on enlarging the bar with its open-air patio, with the patio trough urinal built at about the same time.
A beer bust here raised money for the documentary that became The Times of Harvey Milk, which won the Academy Award for best documentary in 1985.
The Bare Chest Calendar contest moved here from the closed Arena bar and was turned into an AIDS charity fundraiser; it stayed until 1999.
Tom of Finland attended an AIDS fundraiser here at which his work was shown, signed and auctioned; he returned in 1988 for a benefit for the Tom of Finland Foundation.
The bar held a fundraiser for Pat Norman, the first African-American lesbian to run for the Board of Supervisors, raising $1,500.
The bar changed hands and was renamed the Eagle Tavern, the sale requiring that “Eagle” stay in the name.
Thursday Night Live, a weekly rock and punk night, replaced the Bare Chest Calendar contests, which moved to the Powerhouse; bands such as Pansy Division played here often.
The Eagle Tavern closed, and much of its interior lighting and artwork was moved to the Hole in the Wall Saloon on Folsom Street.

New owners bought the bar and brought the building up to code, with structural and electrical upgrades, removal of the horseshoe bar, an accessible bathroom and entrance, and a new roof, before reopening it as the SF Eagle.
A tall metal flagpole flying the Leather flag was put up on the patio after the flag stopped being displayed at the Castro Muni station.
The San Francisco Eagle was entered on the city’s Legacy Business Registry.
Designated San Francisco Landmark No. 295, San Francisco Eagle Bar.

unknowns: The Eagle's opening is dated both 1982 and 8 April 1981, with a grand opening on 12–14 May 1981.

notable_residents.name: Bob Damron
notable_residents.detail: Bob Damron, author of the Damron gay travel guides, opened the bar as one of its two first owners; the partnership kept it until 1998.

notable_residents.name: Terry Thompson
notable_residents.detail: Terry Thompson managed the bar, creating the Sunday beer busts, the Leather and Feathers contest and other fundraisers that raised over $5 million for AIDS charities; he died on 5 November 1994.

notable_residents.name: Alan Selby
notable_residents.detail: Alan Selby, “Daddy Alan”, founder of Mr. S Leather, staged his Leather Daddy contests and AIDS fundraising auctions here; about 400 people gathered at the bar to mark his death.

notable_residents.name: Robert Uyvari
notable_residents.detail: Robert Uyvari, the Wisconsin-born homoerotic artist who designed the Eagle’s poster and T-shirt graphic, had the bar’s first art exhibition; he died of AIDS in 1986.
